title: Biblical Hospitality in the Church
definition: Biblical Hospitality in the Church is the welcoming, generous, and Christlike care shown to believers, strangers, and those in need.
summary: Hospitality displays Gospel welcome through practical love.
christFocus: Jesus Christ welcomed sinners and teaches His people to receive others with grace and truth.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Biblical Hospitality in the Church teaches that Christ does not redeem people into isolation but into a gathered, accountable, worshiping, serving, and mission-shaped people. The Church belongs to Jesus, is formed by the Gospel, and is strengthened by the Word, prayer, ordinances, fellowship, and Spirit-empowered service.

This doctrine helps believers see the Church as more than a place to attend. It is the household of God, the body of Christ, and a visible witness to the grace, holiness, unity, and truth of the Lord.

The specific emphasis here is hospitality displays gospel welcome through practical love.. A healthy church life displays Christ's care for His people and His mission to the world.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because many people treat church as optional, consumer-driven, or disconnected from discipleship. Biblical Hospitality in the Church calls believers back to Christ's design for His people, where worship, truth, love, accountability, service, and mission are held together.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Participate in church life with humility and faithfulness. Let biblical hospitality in the church move you to serve, forgive, gather, pray, give, submit to Scripture, care for others, and help the body of Christ grow in love and maturity.
